title: JS/TS effect patterns: align with actual ref representation
description:
Effect patterns for JS/TS (added in sutra/268) use source-like prefixes (`fetch(`, `document.`, `console.log`, `axios.`, `.then(`, `process.exit`) but the JS parser records call refs differently — bare callee names with the receiver stored separately. For example `console.log()` is recorded as name=`log` with receiver=`console`, `fetch()` as just `fetch`, and `process.env` isn't a call ref at all.

As a result, most JS/TS effect patterns will silently never match during effect enrichment, making the FCA effect detection inert for JS/TS.

Options:
1. Make effect enrichment receiver-aware (join receiver + name before prefix matching)
2. Emit qualified unresolved call chains from the JS/TS parsers
3. Adjust patterns to match the actual extracted ref shape (bare names)

Option 1 is probably cleanest — it keeps patterns readable and fixes the mismatch at the matching layer rather than the extraction layer.

Needs tests: `fetch()`, `axios.get()`, `console.log()`, `document.querySelector()`, `process.env`, and promise/await cases.

acceptance_criteria.text: JS effect patterns match actual call refs emitted by the JS parser
At minimum: fetch(), console.log(), document.querySelector() produce correct effect attributes
Tests cover effect enrichment for JS/TS code

execution_record: Option 1 from the ticket (receiver-aware matching) implemented. The unresolved-ref matching now joins receiver.name into a qualified candidate before prefix matching. Also added p.ends_with('.') to the boundary check so namespace prefixes like \"document.\" correctly match \"document.querySelector\". Fixed JS_EFFECT_PATTERNS: \"fetch(\" → \"fetch\", removed \"await\" and \".then(\" → \"then\". Five new tests cover: multi-pattern qualified matching, false-positive rejection (myObj.log ≠ console.log), process.exit, bare fetch, and then via receiver.
root_cause: JS parser records member calls with bare callee name + separate receiver field (e.g. name=\"log\", receiver=\"console\"), but the unresolved-ref matching path in enrich_with_effects only checked unresolved_name against patterns. Patterns like \"console.log\" never matched because unresolved_name was just \"log\". Additionally, JS_EFFECT_PATTERNS contained source-syntax artifacts (trailing parens in \"fetch(\", leading dot in \".then(\") that could never match extracted ref shapes.
